relevance_note: Three patients with heterozygous TNFAIP3 missense variants and their carrier parents are described individually, e.g. "He had a heterozygous c.574G>A (p.Glu192Lys) variant of TNFAIP3."
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Table 1 has patients as columns (column header 'Patient no.', columns P1, P2, P3); Table 2 has variants as columns. Labels: the text uses 'Patient 1/2/3' more often than the table's 'P1/P2/P3', so rule 1 gives 'Patient 1' etc. Relatives in scope: the father of Patient 1 (same variant, symptomatic), the mother of Patient 2 and the father of Patient 3 (same variant, asymptomatic). The other parent of each patient was sequenced ('Sanger sequencing was performed for the patients and their parents'; WES of patient 3 and her parents) but no result or other detail is given for them individually, so they get no rows. Relatives' variant strings come from the patient's printed variant plus the 'same variant' statement; zygosity, inheritance, pathogenicity and functional fields are left not reported for relatives (D-29). Patient 2's two heterozygous MEFV variants are recorded as separate rows; the authors do not classify them. Variants used only as assay constructs (Phe127Cys, Lys417Serfs*4, Cys243Tyr, Met476Ile, Thr647Pro, Gln709His, Gln709del) and previously reported patients in refs [5], [10]-[12] are not described as individuals here and get no rows. cohort_size_as_stated = 3 (the three patients studied); Patient 1's variant was found among 55 patients screened at Gifu University Hospital, a screening pool not otherwise described. Table 1 'Autoantibody | No' for P1 and P2 read as explicit absence of autoantibodies (a word, not an undefined symbol). Supplementary Table S1 (flow cytometry) was converted without table markup: columns are normal range 2-6 years, P1, normal range >=20 years, P2, P3; only values the legend marks as out of range (bold with arrow) are recorded as observed; values within range were not recorded as excluded. Normal-finding rows (D-27): P1 'no abnormalities in neutrophil function, lymphocyte fraction, or immunoglobulin levels'. 'Lacked any symptoms' for two carrier parents is recorded as one excluded row and excludes no specific checklist item. Possible inconsistency: Patient 2 had fever 'with a high level of serum CRP' but 'Serum inflammatory reactants were negative during the intermittent episodes of fever'; read as the intervals between attacks, so the checklist keeps elevated markers observed, and both rows are emitted. Patient 1's repeated tonsillitis/bronchitis: no pathogens were detected during fever episodes, so 'recurrent infections' is left not reported. Father of Patient 1's 'recurrent stomatitis' is not stated as ulcers, so oral ulcers is not reported. Patient 3's CNS checklist item is observed from athetoid cerebral palsy (after neonatal cardiopulmonary arrest) and epilepsy; her single fever at 24 years is not recorded as recurrent fever. No stacked (' / ') cells in this paper.
